verdictStatement.summary: v12 is the strongest artifact in this chain and most of what it claims I reproduced by execution and could not break. THE OBJECT ANCHOR IS REAL: I rebuilt ep11.review-independent.json's blocking RX1 in my own spelling and confirmed BOTH directions — inside check-evaluation-proof-v11.py's route region it produces a BYTE-IDENTICAL green banner at exit 0 while 7 of 7 pinned verdicts come out of check-c2.py, and inside v12's own route region the same region is caught by A-6 with seven EP12-ANSWER findings naming the seat and installationIntact 0 of 7. I could not defeat the `is` comparison: the seat is a binding, the anchor is an object, and every seat rewrite, wrap, replay and module-accessor spelling I tried is reported rather than believed. The preserved v10/v11 work reproduces digit for digit by execution (regime A 345/93/252/504 -> 8 admitted / 0 moving; regime B 164/51/113/226 -> 9 admitted / 5 moving / 3 beneath a byte-identical seal; admissionDescriptor.schemaVersion moving all six identities; oracle cardinality 4; family 14; v10's own checking layer 0 findings). --selftest is 54/54 rejected BY THE RULE EACH ONE NAMES, and I broke it myself in both directions. My own exhaustive float/bool sweep of v12's own contract admits exactly 4 of 161 cases and those 4 are precisely the four positions the candidate already publishes as silently admitted. BUT THE PUBLISHED SCOPE IS FALSE. answerProvenance.scopeStatement — enforced verbatim by the checker and printed as three lines of the banner — says the property IS established against a hostile route region and is NOT established only against one that reads or writes the guard's stack frame or the closure cells of its servers. I built two route regions that do NEITHER. They read no frame, no closure cell, no dunder, no sys, no getattr/setattr; they write no seat; they name nothing the introspection tripwire enumerates; they use no primitive the candidate's own in-scope variants do not already use. They compare the object at the declared accessor's seat against the object that was there on their first call, serve honestly when the guard is looking and check-c2.py's answer when it is not, and repair the one shared-ledger cell that would otherwise drift. MEASURED: `python3 -I -B ev_md2.py evaluation-proof.v12.json` and `ev_md3.py` each exit 0 with a banner that is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the honest run's, every answer-provenance counter at 21/21/21/21/21 with allRulesHeld True, installationIntact 7 of 7, recordParityHeld 7, anchorsUnmoved True, zero findings from every guard, introspectionSites [], escapedEveryGuard unchanged at the three declared variants, and --selftest returning SELFTEST-PASS — while 7 of 7 pinned validation verdicts are produced by check-c2.py and 0 of 7 by check-c2-v4.py. That is the same defect v11 was rejected for in IR-EP11-02: an ENUMERATION standing in for a property. v12 makes that argument itself about its own tripwire and then commits it in the one place it cannot afford to.

blockers.title: answerProvenance.scopeStatement and the banner's three scope lines are FALSE: they characterise the escape as frame/closure-cell tampering, and a route region that reads neither — comparing only the seat object it saw on its first call — exits 0 with a BYTE-IDENTICAL green banner while 7/7 pinned verdicts are produced by check-c2.py
blockers.statement: check-evaluation-proof-v12.py enforces SCOPE_STATEMENT verbatim (verify_answer_provenance: 'answerProvenance.scopeStatement must carry, verbatim, the boundary this property is scoped by') and prints it as the banner's SCOPE line. It reads: 'This property is established against a hostile ROUTE REGION. It is NOT established against a route region that reads or writes this guard's own stack frame, or the closure cells of the servers it installs: variants AX6, AX9 and RX2c do exactly that ... and are MEASURED to defeat every scored guard.' The second sentence is an ENUMERATION of an exception set, and by construction the first sentence asserts the property holds against every hostile route region outside that set. I falsified it. EVASION MD2 and its more minimal sibling MD3, mine, not among the twenty-five: on its first call the region records `seat = authority.c2v4().validate_plan_intent` and the ledger's UNWRAPPED superseded original, both by ordinary attribute access on the two objects the route region is handed by design. On every later call it re-reads the seat and compares with `is`. When the object at the seat is NOT the one it first saw, the guard is measuring — the anchored server is installed, or a sentinel is — and the region calls it and returns its result unaltered, so A-2, A-3 and A-8 hold honestly and by construction. When the object at the seat IS the one it first saw, nobody is looking, and the region returns the SUPERSEDED module's answer taken through the original it captured before any poisoning, whitelisting to the repaired answer at every position where the two instruments can diverge so the differential oracle sees agreement everywhere. MD2 then repairs the single cell that would otherwise drift — the shared-ledger agreement the guard publishes beside A-2 — by appending a ServedCall inside the answer guard's own unanchored window, identified by the ledger's own label stack; MD3 does the same thing without any label or forgery at all, by OVERWRITING the result field of the entry the genuine call had already created, so no entry count anywhere moves. Both are confined to the ROUTE-REGION: I asserted programmatically that the text before # ROUTE-REGION-BEGIN and after # ROUTE-REGION-END is byte-identical to check-evaluation-proof-v12.py, and I asserted programmatically that the region contains none of _getframe, f_locals, f_back, __closure__, cell_contents, __code__, __globals__, traceback, inspect, sys, getattr, setattr, vars, globals or __dict__. It writes no seat, so A-6 has nothing to report. MEASURED END TO END, from a directory holding only the 30 pinned inputs plus the candidate and the checker: `python3 -I -B ev_md2.py evaluation-proof.v12.json` exits 0 and prints a banner BYTE-IDENTICAL to the unmodified checker's, including 'ANSWER PROVENANCE ESTABLISHED ... 21 ... (A-1); 21 ARE the object produced by the function object the SHA-256-verified bytes defined, compared by `is` against this guard's own frame-local anchor (A-2); 21 ... (A-3); 21 ... (A-4); 7 ... (A-5); 7 vectors found the load-time installation still identical before, during and after the drive (A-6); 21 ... (A-7); anchors unmoved True, record parity held for 7 vectors (A-8)' and the unqualified 'ESCAPED EVERY SCORED GUARD [AX6, AX9, RX2c]'. ev_md3.py is byte-identical in banner too. Reading the guard's own counters directly rather than the banner: answer-provenance findings 0; vectors 7, apisPerVector 3, expectedPerRuleTotal 21, independentValueAgreements 21, anchoredObjectAgreements 21, sharedLedgerAgreements 21, repairedSentinelFlowed 21, supersededSentinelIgnored 21, gateAgreements 7, installationIntact 7, unanchoredValueAgreements 21, recordParityHeld 7, evaluationErrors 0, allRulesHeld True, anchorsUnmoved True — every value identical to the honest run's. call provenance 28/21/1/0 with zero findings; total heavy findings 0; oracle 1656 executed / 0 mismatches / cardinality 4; route_introspection_scan introspectionSites []; c2_route_scan referencesOutsideDeclaredClosure [], unroutedSitesInsideJoin [], authorityRoutedSites 3; regionDefinitions 3; installationDefectsAfterDrive []; rebound module globals []; predecessor-defeat control unchanged at defeated=True / caught=True / {'check-c2.py': 7} against {'check-c2-v4.py': 7}; and `python3 -I -B ev_md2.py --selftest` returns SELFTEST-PASS with all 54 mutations rejected. Against that, my INDEPENDENT seat attribution — every reachable spelling of validate_plan_intent on both module objects and both ledger originals wrapped in retaining markers, driven in the production ordering, reading nothing either instrument publishes — reports the validation verdict for 7 of 7 pinned vectors produced by check-c2.py and 0 of 7 by check-c2-v4.py, against 7 of 7 by check-c2-v4.py for the unmodified checker in the identical harness. WHY THIS IS BLOCKING AND NOT AN OBSERVATION. It is not that the class is undisclosed — RES-EP12-16's second consequence says in terms that 'a region that behaves differently when observed is bounded here only by A-7's value agreement and by A-6's identity checks, not by anything stronger', and that sentence is true and is to v12's credit. It is that the boundary the instrument ENFORCES and PRINTS is a different, narrower, and false one. A reader of the banner is told exactly one thing breaks the green — a frame or closure-cell read — and that is cheap to exclude by inspection. My regions are excluded by that inspection and defeat the property anyway. This is IR-EP11-02's defect exactly: v11 was rejected because a spelling ENUMERATION stood where a property was needed, and RES-EP12-04 makes that argument itself — 'it is an ENUMERATION and it is NOT a proof'. v12 removed the enumeration from the guard set and then reintroduced the same shape one level up, as an enumeration of three variant names standing for the escape CLASS. Two further facts sharpen it: the escape set is bound as a residual measurement to those three names (RES-EP12-02.boundValueText), so the artifact's own binding machinery certifies an incomplete set as this run's measurement; and RES-EP12-16, the only place the class is disclosed at all, can itself be hollowed to a padded stub of anchors plus its bound number while the checker stays green — I did it and measured exit 0.

blockers.requiredToClear: Any ONE of the following would clear it, and the third is cheap. (a) CLOSE IT: make the anchored window unannounced, so the region cannot tell measurement from production — the natural spelling is to keep this guard's servers installed for the WHOLE drive including the A-7 and call-provenance windows, so there is no unobserved window to behave differently in, and to make A-7's control run in a subprocess or against a second Authority the region has never seen. (b) BIND THE UNANCHORED ANSWER BY IDENTITY as well as by value: require the object the unanchored drive returns to be the object the ledger's own wrapper returned for that call — `unanchored[key] is entry.result` for the genuine entry — rather than merely equal to the reference value, and make the ledger entry list append-only from the region's side, so MD3's one-line overwrite is a finding rather than a repair. (c) SCOPE IT CORRECTLY, which I would accept as clearing this blocker on its own: replace the enumeration in SCOPE_STATEMENT and in the banner with the PROPERTY boundary that RES-EP12-16 already states — that A-2 holds only inside an anchored window this guard opens and announces, that outside it the answer is bound by value alone, and that therefore ANY route region which behaves differently when observed escapes, of which AX6, AX9 and RX2c are three built instances and not the class — and enumerate MD2/MD3 in the battery as a fourth declared escape so the escapedEveryGuard binding names a set that is not measurably incomplete. I want to be explicit that I am NOT ruling that a green exit with 7/7 wrong-module verdicts is unacceptable regardless of disclosure: see centralClaimAdjudications claim 4. I am ruling that the disclosure v12 enforces and prints does not cover the class, and that an enumeration of three variant names is not a characterisation of an escape class — which is v12's own argument about its own tripwire, applied to v12.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: Is the anchor genuinely an object rather than a seat?
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: UPHELD. The anchor is an object, the `is` comparison holds, and I could not defeat it by any seat manipulation.
whatIAttacked: seat substitution through the declared accessor (my own RX1, ev_rx1r.py): CAUGHT. installation_status compares getattr(row['module'], api) against the load-time capture by `is` and reports 'no longer the ledger wrapper installed at load time'; 7 findings, installationIntact 0 of 7 against a published 7, allRulesHeld False, exit 1.

substitute the module object before capture: NOT REACHABLE. capture_installation runs in heavy_measurements BEFORE the first route-region call this run makes, and the installation is a local threaded by parameter, not a module-level table — the docstring says exactly why and it is true in the shipped bytes.

make the substitute the same object: IMPOSSIBLE without the anchor, and the anchor is a guard frame local. A-2 compares witnessed.callee is anchors[api], and the server reads its cell into a local and records THAT, so a rewritten cell yields a record naming the substitute. The stated reason a seat rewrite fails is correct and I verified it by reading _anchored_server and by measuring RX1, RX3, RX4 and RX6 against the guard.

poison the guard's private instances by swapping the verified bytes: BLOCKED. _private_module re-hashes snapshots[name] against ALL_PINS before executing, so authority._snapshots (which IS reachable, and which the Authority docstring honestly says is reachable) cannot be used to build a dishonest anchor. Rewriting ALL_PINS as well would move the anchor's code fingerprint away from the ledger original's, which the guard cross-checks (served_defects) and reports.

identity-preserving proxy, id recycling, argument-fingerprint confusion, cross-window replay: all fail. The witness retains the result object; argfp is canonical-JSON SHA-256 of args[0]; record parity requires exactly one record per api per window at depth 0 over THIS vector's fingerprint, which is what closes RX4's replay against a corpus that carries one distinct PlanIntent.

exception tracebacks, __self__, bound-method identity, functools wrappers: nothing here is a bound method or a wrapper; anchors[api] is a plain function and the guard checks isinstance(..., types.FunctionType) before anchoring.
centralClaimAdjudications.whereItLeaks: The anchor object is reachable, but not by a path that defeats A-2. _exec_verified registers every private instance in sys.modules under a predictable prefix, and after a guard run sys.modules carries _ep12_anchor_2_check_c2_v4_py, _ep12_anchor3_3_check_c2_py and _ep12_reference_4_check_c2_v4_py — neither a stack frame nor a closure cell. See IR-EP12-NB-04. It does not change this adjudication because reaching the anchor does not let a region produce an object the anchor did not produce.
centralClaimAdjudications.assessment: This is the genuine repair of IR-EP11-01 and it is exactly as advertised. The distinction between a binding and an object is correctly drawn and correctly implemented. My blocker does not touch it: MD2 defeats the property by never contesting the anchor at all.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: Reproduce the v11 defeat and the v12 catch
centralClaimAdjudications.v11Defeated: I wrote my own seat-substitution region (RX1R) from the published description rather than copying the candidate's _RX1_SEAT string, inserted it into check-evaluation-proof-v11.py's ROUTE-REGION with prefix and suffix asserted byte-identical, and ran it. `python3 -I -B v11_rx1r.py evaluation-proof.v11.json` exits 0 and its banner is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the unmodified check-evaluation-proof-v11.py's banner, including 'ANSWER PROVENANCE ESTABLISHED ... 21 ARE the object that module produced for this vector (A-2)'. My independent attribution reports {'check-c2.py': 7} for the variant and {'check-c2-v4.py': 7} for the unmodified predecessor in the identical harness. Every element of the claim reproduces: full green banner, 21/21/21/21/21 + 7 gates, allRulesHeld, oracle 0 mismatches, introspectionSites [].
centralClaimAdjudications.v12Catches: The same region inside v12 exits 1 with seven EP12-ANSWER findings, each reading 'the served-module installation this run captured at load time no longer holds: [check-c2-v4.py.validate_plan_intent is no longer the ledger wrapper installed at load time] (A-6)', exactly the text the brief quotes, plus 'answerProvenance publishes installationIntact=7; this run measured 0' and 'not every answer-provenance rule held'. The catch is A-6, it is behavioural, and it reads no source.
centralClaimAdjudications.assessment: The central repair claim is true and I confirmed it in both directions with my own bytes.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: predecessorDefeatControl — can it be made vacuous?
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: PARTLY. It cannot go silent, but its CONSEQUENCE half is unenforced and I made that half vacuous and stayed green.
centralClaimAdjudications.whatCannotGoVacuous: heavy_measurements adds a finding if predecessor['error'] is set, if predecessorIsDefeated is not truthy, or if thisInstrumentCatchesIt is not truthy. So the control cannot silently stop running, cannot swallow an exception, and cannot report the predecessor as un-defeated or this instrument as blind without producing a finding. I confirmed the three findings exist in the shipped bytes and that verify_predecessor_control additionally strict_equals the whole published block against the measured one, so no field of it may be edited. It rebuilds RX1 inside v11's SHA-256-verified bytes on every run, seeds v11's own scan cache with those bytes so the predecessor never re-opens its path, and drives both instruments in the production ordering. Nothing is transcribed. That is a genuinely novel and load-bearing construct and it works.
centralClaimAdjudications.whatIMadeVacuous: The attribution — the half that establishes the CONSEQUENCE, that the verdicts served are check-c2.py's — is measured and published but nothing requires it to be true. I disabled the seat-attribution instrument alone (replacing _seat_attribution with one that returns UNATTRIBUTED) and left everything else untouched. MEASURED: predecessorIsDefeated True, thisInstrumentCatchesIt True, variantRoutesEveryPinnedVerdictToTheSupersededEncoder FALSE, unmodifiedPredecessorRoutesEveryPinnedVerdictToTheRepairedModule FALSE, thisInstrumentDetectsRatherThanPrevents FALSE, verdictsUnderTheVariantBy {'UNATTRIBUTED': 7}, and ZERO findings mentioning PREDECESSOR. Republishing the degraded block verbatim in the candidate gives check() -> 0 findings, a green run, and a banner that prints 'the pinned verdicts it serves are attributed {'UNATTRIBUTED': 7} against {'UNATTRIBUTED': 7}'. So if the attribution instrument ever silently degrades — a future C-2 module returning an interned or cached object would do it — the control collapses to 'v11 is silent, v12 is noisy' without proving that the thing v11 is silent about is a wrong answer, and no rule notices.
centralClaimAdjudications.shippedRunIsHonest: On the shipped bytes the control measures {'check-c2.py': 7} against {'check-c2-v4.py': 7} and I reproduced both independently. This is drift risk, not a false claim in the shipped bytes. Recorded as IR-EP12-NB-01.
centralClaimAdjudications.requiredToClose: require variantRoutesEveryPinnedVerdictToTheSupersededEncoder, unmodifiedPredecessorRoutesEveryPinnedVerdictToTheRepairedModule and thisInstrumentDetectsRatherThanPrevents to be TRUE, the same way predecessorIsDefeated and thisInstrumentCatchesIt already are.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: THE DECLARED ESCAPE — my ruling on the boundary
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: THE APPROACH IS LEGITIMATE; THIS INSTANCE OF IT IS NOT. The scoping is prominent and honest in intent but WRONG IN CONTENT, and that is what I find blocking.
centralClaimAdjudications.whereILand: I rule, explicitly and first, that a green exit with 7/7 wrong-module verdicts is NOT automatically unacceptable. A checker cannot defend against arbitrary modification of itself, and I treated no mutation of answer_provenance_guard, ALL_PINS, check() or the checking layer as a finding. More than that: I accept that a class can be legitimately carved out of a published property by DECLARING it, provided the declaration describes the CLASS and not three instances of it, provided the declaration is where the reader looks, and provided nothing else published depends on the class being closed. v12 gets two of those three right, and the two it gets right are real advances I want on the record. Removing the introspection tripwire from the scored guard set is exactly the correct answer to IR-EP11-02 and it is enforced structurally, by GUARD_REGISTRY, not by intention: the tripwire publishes scored=false, RX2c is built and measured escaping it on every run, and no property rests on it — I verified by mutation that emptying escapedEveryGuard is rejected and that the scope and anchor statements are enforced verbatim. Putting the scope in the BANNER as three lines rather than only in a residual is the direct repair of IR-EP11-NB-08 and of RET-EP11-03's own subject, and it is the single most reader-facing improvement in this document.
centralClaimAdjudications.whyItStillFails: The scope that is enforced and printed is an ENUMERATION of an exception set — 'a route region that reads or writes this guard's own stack frame, or the closure cells of the servers it installs: variants AX6, AX9 and RX2c' — and the enumeration is incomplete by measurement. My MD2 and MD3 read no frame and no closure cell, and the run is byte-identically green while every pinned verdict comes from check-c2.py. The reader who does what the banner tells them to do — exclude frame and cell reads, which is a cheap grep — draws a false conclusion. That is the failure mode this corpus has rejected three times running, and it is the SAME shape as IR-EP11-02: an enumeration standing where a property is needed. v12 argues this itself, about its own tripwire, in RES-EP12-04 and in the Section 6 header, and then commits it in the scopeStatement. Two things make it worse rather than better: RES-EP12-02 BINDS the escape set to those three names as this run's measurement, so the artifact's own binding machinery certifies a measurably incomplete set; and RES-EP12-16 — the only place in the whole document where my class is disclosed — can be hollowed to a padded stub of anchors plus its bound number with the checker green, which I measured.
centralClaimAdjudications.whatWouldClearIt: State the boundary as the property. RES-EP12-16 already contains the correct sentence — 'a region that behaves differently when observed is bounded here only by A-7's value agreement and by A-6's identity checks, not by anything stronger'. Put THAT in scopeStatement and in the banner, in place of the three variant names, and enumerate MD2/MD3 as declared escapes. Then the green means what it says, the enumeration is illustrative rather than definitional, and I would not find this blocking.
centralClaimAdjudications.myOwnUnenumeratedFrameVariant: BUILT AND MEASURED, and the candidate's account of this class is CORRECT. I wrote two frame tampers of my own with spellings distinct from AX6, AX9 and RX2c: FT2/FT3 take the frame from a traceback reached with operator.attrgetter over attribute names assembled from string constants, walk f_back, read the guard's local by an assembled name, and OVERWRITE both the honest witness record's result and the shared-ledger entry's result rather than forging new ones. MEASURED: route_introspection_scan reports introspectionSites [] — my spellings escape the 49-identifier enumeration, as declared — and the answer-provenance guard returns ZERO findings with anchoredObjectAgreements 21, sharedLedgerAgreements 21, installationIntact 7 and allRulesHeld True, while 7 of 7 pinned verdicts come from check-c2.py. So the class does defeat every scored guard exactly as published. BOTH of my frame variants nevertheless exit 1, and — confirming the candidate's own statement that this is an accidental defence — NEVER through a guard: FT3's five findings are per-variant catch-matrix drift (differentialOracle 10 -> 11) plus the own-constant-leaf battery cascade, and FT2 additionally trips the integer-guard tripwire on the construct `item.depth == 0`. The candidate states in RES-EP12-02 that its author refined a whole-file variant of this class until no published count moved and it exits 0 green; I did not complete that refinement, because MD2/MD3 already reach the stronger result — a byte-identical green banner with zero drift — with no frame at all. I record the negative as a negative: I confirmed the guard-silence half of the claim exactly and did not independently confirm the zero-drift half.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: Residual binding — try to gut them
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: MATERIALLY STRONGER THAN v11 AND EVERY NAMED ATTACK FAILS, BUT PADDING STILL GUTS — which the candidate itself discloses
centralClaimAdjudications.whatIsRepaired: Five of the six attacks the brief names are closed and I confirmed each by execution. nonBlockingObservations.observation: The predecessor-defeat control's CONSEQUENCE half is measured and published but not required to hold. heavy_measurements enforces predecessor['error'] absent, predecessorIsDefeated true and thisInstrumentCatchesIt true — all three genuinely, and I confirmed each — but nothing enforces variantRoutesEveryPinnedVerdictToTheSupersededEncoder, unmodifiedPredecessorRoutesEveryPinnedVerdictToTheRepairedModule or thisInstrumentDetectsRatherThanPrevents. I disabled the seat-attribution instrument alone and measured all three FALSE, verdictsUnderTheVariantBy {'UNATTRIBUTED': 7}, zero PREDECESSOR findings, and check() green after republishing the degraded block. The banner would then print 'the pinned verdicts it serves are attributed {'UNATTRIBUTED': 7}' beside the word DEFEATED. Requiring the three booleans the same way the other two are required closes it in three lines.

The residual rule is a minimum length plus an anchor grep plus a verbatim bound value, so a residual reduced to its anchors and its bound number and padded to length passes with all meaning removed. I gutted six and the checker exited 0 with no findings each time, including RES-EP12-02 (the threat-model boundary) and RES-EP12-16 (the only disclosure of my blocker's class). This is materially stronger than the predecessor — hollowing, softening the bound value, and demotion to text-only are all now rejected, and both of ep11.review-independent.json's retraction holes are genuinely closed — and RES-EP12-17 discloses the remaining gap in terms ('Binding is not meaning: a determined author can still pad around a correct number'), which is why this is non-blocking. A rule that also required a declared minimum count of distinct sentences, or bound each residual to TWO independent measurements, would raise the cost again.

RES-EP12-11's measured claim about check-completeness.py is FALSE, and it is the one residual v12 declares text-only on the ground that it cannot measure another checker's exit code. It states that check-completeness.py 'exits 1 on ONE cross-cutting open finding, and that finding is IR-C2V4-01', and that R2-FINAL-03 was the cause only 'before that adjudication landed, so the cause has moved'. MEASURED on this host at these bytes: check-completeness.py exits 1 printing BOTH — 'open: IR-C2V4-01' on the C-2 surface row, which drives seal readiness to 8 of 11, and separately 'cross-cutting open findings: 1 / open: R2-FINAL-03'. Both terms of the exit condition are live. R2-FINAL-03 is not stale and is precisely the one cross-cutting finding the residual reassigns to IR-C2V4-01. This is a prose assertion standing where a record should be, inside a document whose thesis is that a count is not a record and a prose assertion is not a record. Nothing in v12 depends on it, which is why it is non-blocking; it should be restated to name both findings in their correct roles.

The guard's private instances are reachable through sys.modules, which is neither a stack frame nor a closure cell, so RES-EP12-02's characterisation of how they can be reached is understated in a second, independent way. _exec_verified does `sys.modules[name] = module` with name = f'{prefix}_{serial}_{sanitised filename}', so after a guard run sys.modules carries _ep12_anchor_2_check_c2_v4_py, _ep12_anchor3_3_check_c2_py and _ep12_reference_4_check_c2_v4_py — measured, not inferred. Reaching the anchor instance does not by itself defeat A-2, and the introspection tripwire does flag the identifier `sys` (I confirmed: a region that names it exits 1 on EP12-SCAN), so I am recording this rather than raising it as a second blocker; but the tripwire is by design not a scored guard and an unenumerated spelling of the same reach is the RX2c exercise repeated. Two specific consequences are worth closing regardless: A-8 checks the anchored instance's FUNCTION bindings only, so a non-function module global of the anchor instance is unchecked; and the A-1 REFERENCE instance has no integrity check at all — reference.validate_plan_intent is an attribute lookup at call time and nothing compares it against what the verified bytes defined. Deleting each private module from sys.modules immediately after _exec_verified returns, and extending the A-8 binding check to the reference instance, would cost a handful of lines.

The introspection tripwire is correctly excluded from the SCORED guard set and no published property rests on it — that part is real and structurally enforced by GUARD_REGISTRY. But it still produces a finding on an ordinary run and therefore still gates the exit code: a route region that names one of the 49 identifiers exits 1 on 'EP12-SCAN: the route region names an introspection primitive', which I measured. 'Not a scored guard' and 'does not affect the verdict' are different statements and the document uses the first in places a reader may take as the second. This is not a defect — an unscored tripwire that still refuses is a reasonable design — but the distinction deserves one sentence, because the whole point of RES-EP12-04 is that the enumeration must not be load-bearing, and today it is load-bearing for the exit code even though it is not load-bearing for any property.

Confirming the candidate's own honesty about its accidental defences, with numbers. Both of my unenumerated frame tampers defeat every scored guard completely — answer-provenance findings 0, anchoredObjectAgreements 21, sharedLedgerAgreements 21, installationIntact 7, allRulesHeld True, introspectionSites [] — and both exit 1 anyway, never through a guard: through per-variant catch-matrix drift (differentialOracle 10 -> 11) cascading into the own-constant-leaf battery, and in one case additionally through the integer-guard tripwire, which flags the construct `item.depth == 0` inside the route region because 'item' is in WIRE_SOURCED_HINTS. That last one is a genuinely accidental defence of the most incidental kind — the frame-tamper class is caught by a scan looking for the LB-C2-01 bug — and it disappears if the attacker writes `not item.depth`. The candidate's statement that these exit 1 only through published-number drift is therefore accurate and, if anything, generous to itself.

answerProvenance.positiveControl and predecessorDefeatControl are compared wholesale with strict_equal, which is type-exact and therefore genuinely catches a floated or booled leaf inside them — but the finding names the BLOCK rather than the leaf. 33 of the 161 cases in my float/bool sweep are rejected this way. No case escapes, so this is a message-granularity observation rather than a coverage gap; I record it because the corpus standard is that a rejection should name the position it rejects, and because a future reader auditing these two blocks by grepping finding text will not find their leaves named.

Ordinary v12 run ~28 s; --selftest ~27 s; my float/bool sweep ~4 min; each end-to-end evasion run ~28 s.
